title: Longest Common Subsequence
oneLinerQuestion: Find the length of the longest sub-sequence shared between two strings.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) problem asks for the length of the longest subsequence present in both string text1 and string text2. A subsequence is derived by deleting zero or more characters without changing the relative order of the remaining characters. A brute-force recursive tree branching on every character comparison takes exponential O(2^(M + N)) time due to overlapping subproblems. Dynamic programming reduces this to polynomial time using a 2D grid `dp`, where `dp[i][j]` represents the length of the longest common subsequence between suffixes `text1[i...]` and `text2[j...]`. If the characters at the current indices match (`text1[i] === text2[j]`), we greedily consume both characters and add 1 to the diagonal subproblem: `1 + dp[i+1][j+1]`. If they do not match, the optimal answer must come from either skipping `text1[i]` or skipping `text2[j]`, taking `max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1])`.

- Step 1: String Lengths & DP Matrix Allocation — Let `M = text1.length` and `N = text2.length`. Allocate a 2D array `dp` of size `(M + 1) x (N + 1)` filled with zeros: `const dp = Array.from({ length: M + 1 }, () => new Array(N + 1).fill(0))`. The extra row and column act as base cases representing empty string suffixes.

- Step 2: Base Case Initialization — Suffixes where either `i === M` or `j === N` have an LCS length of 0 because an empty string shares no subsequence with any string; these are naturally handled by zero-filling.

- Step 3: Backward Nested Loop Iteration — Iterate backwards through both strings using nested loops: outer loop `for (let i = M - 1; i >= 0; i--)` and inner loop `for (let j = N - 1; j >= 0; j--)`.

- Step 4: Matching Character Transition — Check if the characters match: `if (text1[i] === text2[j])`. If equal, both characters can contribute to the common subsequence: `dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i + 1][j + 1]`.

- Step 5: Mismatched Character Transition — If `text1[i] !== text2[j]`, the optimal choice is the better outcome between dropping the current character of `text1` versus dropping the current character of `text2`: `dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i + 1][j], dp[i][j + 1])`.

- Step 6: Memory Optimization Alternative — Because each row `i` only depends on the row immediately below it (`i + 1`), the table can be space-optimized to two 1D rows (or a single 1D row of size `N + 1` with a temporary diagonal variable), reducing memory to O(min(M, N)).

- Step 7: Termination & Result Return — Once all states are resolved, `dp[0][0]` contains the length of the longest common subsequence for the full strings `text1[0...]` and `text2[0...]`. Return `dp[0][0]`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(M * N) where M is the length of `text1` and N is the length of `text2`, as each cell in the (M + 1) x (N + 1) matrix is filled exactly once in O(1) time. Space Complexity: O(M * N) auxiliary space for the full 2D DP matrix (or O(min(M, N)) if using space-optimized rolling rows).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION longestCommonSubsequence(text1, text2):
    dp = MATRIX(LENGTH(text1) + 1, LENGTH(text2) + 1, 0)
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(text1) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        FOR j FROM LENGTH(text2) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
            IF text1[i] == text2[j] THEN dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i + 1][j + 1]
            ELSE dp[i][j] = MAX(dp[i + 1][j], dp[i][j + 1])
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN dp[0][0]
END FUNCTION
